stem: Soon after labor epidural placement, the fetal tracing develops recurrent late decelerations. Which maternal assessment should the nurse prioritize?

options.D: Maternal urine output over the previous hour.

rationale: Current Open RN/NCBI labor-and-delivery guidance explains that spinal or epidural anesthesia can cause maternal hypotension, which can reduce placental perfusion and contribute to late fetal heart-rate decelerations. The same chapter directs monitoring of fetal heart rate during maternal hypotension because decreased maternal pressure can reduce uteroplacental perfusion and fetal oxygenation. In this immediate post-epidural context, maternal blood pressure is therefore the priority maternal assessment. Temperature, blood glucose, and prior-hour urine output do not assess the most direct acute hemodynamic complication linked to the new late decelerations.
educational_objective: When recurrent late decelerations appear soon after epidural placement, assess maternal blood pressure promptly because neuraxial anesthesia can cause hypotension and reduced uteroplacental perfusion.
source_document_title: Nursing Health Promotion — Chapter 10: Labor & Delivery Care
source_locator: Chapter 10 > Fetal heart-rate decelerations > Late Decelerations: spinal or epidural anesthesia can cause maternal hypotension resulting in placental hypoperfusion. Epidural analgesia monitoring discussion: during hypotension, monitor FHR because hypotension can decrease uteroplacental perfusion and fetal oxygenation. Table 10.5a: late-deceleration interventions include correction of maternal hypotension.
source_claim_supported: Neuraxial anesthesia can cause maternal hypotension that reduces uteroplacental perfusion and contributes to late decelerations, making maternal blood pressure the priority maternal assessment in the immediate post-epidural scenario.

Adjusted final difficulty from hard to medium because the item is a focused post-procedure complication-recognition question with a single direct physiologic link.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Maternal hypotension and late fetal decelerations after epidural

audit_findings.claim_audit: The final rationale uses only the directly stated mechanism: neuraxial anesthesia may cause maternal hypotension, reduced placental perfusion, and fetal late decelerations. No numeric blood-pressure threshold or treatment dose is introduced.

distractor_audit.A: Correct and directly assesses the immediate post-epidural complication linked to late decelerations.
distractor_audit.B: Temperature can matter in labor but does not directly assess the acute hemodynamic complication suggested by the timing.
distractor_audit.C: Blood glucose is not the direct post-epidural mechanism linked to the new late decelerations.
distractor_audit.D: Prior-hour urine output is less immediate and does not directly assess the acute maternal pressure change caused by neuraxial anesthesia.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Given the immediate post-epidural onset and the request for a maternal assessment, only blood pressure directly evaluates the source-supported complication.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are all maternal physiologic assessments and comparable in format; no wording directly repeats the mechanism in the stem.

audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-audited timing, mechanism, all options, NCBI locator, rationale, objective, blueprint, difficulty, ambiguity and cueing. A remained uniquely best.
